claims.text: Eutectic high-entropy alloys have dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Microcrack nucleation at lamellar interfaces causes room-temperature tensile brittleness.
A tailored post-solidification thermomechanical treatment can induce nanoscale precipitates selectively at lamellar interfaces.
Finely dispersed nanoscale precipitates at lamellar interfaces will improve room-temperature tensile strength.
Finely dispersed nanoscale precipitates at lamellar interfaces will improve room-temperature tensile ductility.
Interfacial nanoscale precipitates strengthen inter-lamellar boundaries by enhancing local cohesion.
Interfacial nanoscale precipitates impede microcrack initiation.
Interfacial nanoscale precipitates impede microcrack propagation.
Interfacial nanoscale precipitates improve load transfer across the lamellae.
Improved load transfer and suppression of microcracking mitigate premature failure and enhance ductility.
The treated alloy will have higher yield strength than the as-cast lamellar-colony baseline.
The treated alloy will have higher ultimate tensile strength than the as-cast lamellar-colony baseline.
The treated alloy will have greater room-temperature strain to failure than the as-cast lamellar-colony baseline.
The intervention is beneficial only when precipitate size and spatial distribution are carefully controlled.
Precipitate coarsening or nonuniform precipitation can adversely affect both strength and ductility.
